title: What Do Animals Eat? Bamboo, Leaves and Grass
description:
What do animals eat? Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then find out: a panda's food is almost all bamboo and it grips the stems with a special thumb-like bump, a koala eats almost only eucalyptus leaves and sniffs out its favorites, and a zebra snips grass with its front teeth and can drink more than a gallon of water at one time.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: At least 98% of a giant panda's diet is bamboo; active for roughly 14 hours per day, spending most of this time foraging; grasps bamboo with the front feet, between palm and thumb-like digit (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Giant Panda', Diet & Feeding, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/giantpanda/diet, read Nov 16 2026).

Giant panda: unique thumb-like digit (modified sesamoid bone), enlarged and covered in a tough pad; large, flat molars for grinding bamboo; strong jaw bones and chewing muscles give a bite force higher than any other bear (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Giant Panda', Physical Characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

Koalas feed almost exclusively on leaves of Eucalyptus; smell plays a role in identifying preferred species; koalas rarely drink in the wild and produce dry pellets (water conservation) (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Koala', Diet & Feeding, read Nov 16 2026).

An adult koala spends about 19-20 hours a day sitting or sleeping; a low-energy lifestyle is necessary for an animal that specializes on such a low-energy diet (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Koala', Behavior & Ecology, read Nov 16 2026).

Plains zebras primarily consume grasses (more than 90% of diet), about 50 grass species; incisor teeth crop grasses, cheek teeth grind the food; they immerse their lips below the water surface to drink and may take in more than 4 liters (1 gallon) in a single bout (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Plains Zebra', Diet & Feeding, read Nov 16 2026).
Plains zebras form large herds of several hundred; social grooming: they clean one another's coat and mane (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Plains Zebra', Behavior & Ecology, read Nov 16 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about what animals eat!
What is on the menu today?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Are you hungry for fun facts? Let's go!

segments.name: panda

lines.t: Who eats bamboo, almost all day long?
Is it the panda? Or is it the zebra?

lines: It is the panda!
Here is the fun fact. Almost all of a panda's food is bamboo!
Bamboo leaves, bamboo stems, and yummy bamboo shoots. Crunch, crunch!

lines.t: How does a panda hold its bamboo? Hmm.

lines: With its front paws! A panda has a special bump, like a thumb, to grip the bamboo.
Look! It holds the bamboo tight, and munches away.
close:panda
Bamboo is tough. So a panda has big, flat back teeth, to grind it up.
And strong chewing muscles. A panda's bite is stronger than any other bear's!
A panda is busy for about fourteen hours a day, and spends most of that time finding food and eating.
That is a lot of munching! Munch, munch, munch!
Say it with me. A panda eats bamboo!
close:host
Can you hold bamboo like a panda? Hold it tight, and munch, munch!
Now grind it up with your back teeth. Chomp, chomp!

lines.t: Quick check! What does a panda eat the most? Bamboo? Or fish?

lines: Bamboo! Crunch, crunch. Great job!

short.title: What Does a Panda Eat All Day? Panda Facts

segments.name: koala

lines.t: Who eats the leaves of a tree called eucalyptus?
Is it the koala? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the koala!
Here is the fun fact. A koala eats almost only eucalyptus leaves.
Eucalyptus leaves, every single day. Nibble, nibble!

lines.t: How does a koala find the leaves it likes best? Hmm.

lines: It sniffs them! A koala uses its nose, to find its favorite leaves. Sniff, sniff!
Look at that big, round nose!
close:koala
And here is a surprise. A koala hardly ever drinks water!
Its body is very, very good at saving water. Clever koala!
Eucalyptus leaves do not give a koala much energy. So a koala rests a lot.
A koala sits or sleeps for about twenty hours a day! Shh.
Say it with me. A koala eats eucalyptus leaves!
close:host
Can you sniff like a koala? Sniff, sniff! Which leaf smells the best?
Now hug a tree, and take a little nap. Shh.

lines.t: Quick check! What does a koala eat? Leaves? Or fish?

lines: Leaves! Eucalyptus leaves. You remembered!

short.title: What Does a Koala Eat? Koala Facts for Kids

segments.name: zebra

lines.t: Who eats grass, and has black and white stripes?
Is it the zebra? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the zebra!
Here is the fun fact. Grass is almost all of a zebra's food!
Zebras eat about fifty different kinds of grass. Munch, munch!

lines.t: How does a zebra eat the grass? Hmm.

lines: Its front teeth cut the grass. Snip, snip! And its back teeth grind it up.
Look at the zebra, munching away.
close:zebra
When a zebra is thirsty, it puts its lips under the water, to drink.
A zebra can drink more than one gallon of water, at one time! Gulp, gulp!
Zebras live together in big, big herds. Some herds have hundreds of zebras!
And zebra friends help keep each other clean. They use their teeth, to clean each other's coat and mane. Scratch, scratch!
Say it with me. A zebra eats grass!
close:host
Can you snip like a zebra? Snip, snip, snip, with your front teeth!
Now drink like a zebra. Gulp, gulp, gulp!

lines.t: Quick check! What does a zebra eat? Grass? Or bamboo?

lines: Grass! Munch, munch. Super thinking!

short.title: How Does a Zebra Eat and Drink? Zebra Facts

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three hungry friends. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who grips bamboo with a bump like a thumb?
Who sniffs out its favorite eucalyptus leaves?
Who snips grass with its front teeth?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Munch like a panda. Sniff like a koala. And snip like a zebra!
What is your favorite food?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
